deployNotes: Pure static frontend with no backend, database or cache, so a single web pod is enough.

Build with the repo Dockerfile: the node:20-alpine builder stage should use mirror.gcr.io/library/node:20-alpine, and the runtime stage mirror.gcr.io/library/nginx:alpine, to avoid Docker Hub pull failures on the cluster.
nginx serves the Vite dist output on port 80 (nginx.conf is copied to /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf).
No environment variables are read by the app, so none need to be configured.

productionPlan.summary: Cyberpunk Analytics is a static React and Vite dashboard. It has no backend, database or keys. The repo's Dockerfile builds the bundle with Node and serves the dist folder from nginx on port 80, so one web service is all it needs. The thing that matters most is that the Dockerfile runs `npm ci` but the repo has no package-lock.json, so the build will fail until that is fixed.

decisions.decision: One web service: the nginx image built from the repo Dockerfile, serving the built static site on port 80 at path /
decisions.why: The app is a pure client-side React bundle. Its package.json scripts are only `vite`, `vite build` and `vite preview`, and the Dockerfile ends in nginx serving /usr/share/nginx/html.

decisions.decision: Build with the existing multi-stage Dockerfile at the repo root, after changing `npm ci` to `npm install` and moving both FROM lines to mirror.gcr.io/library images
decisions.why: `npm ci` requires a package-lock.json, and the repo tree has none. Unmirrored Docker Hub base images risk pull failures.

decisions.decision: Port 80, the nginx listen port, is the only port. The Vite dev port 3000 is ignored in production.
decisions.why: nginx.conf listens on 80 and the Dockerfile exposes 80. The vite.config.js server block (0.0.0.0:3000) only affects `npm run dev`.

decisions.decision: No keys or environment variables are needed
decisions.why: The app has no backend and no env vars were found. The service's vars are empty.
Nothing is written at runtime. nginx only serves files baked into the image at build time.

fix_before_production.title: Replace `npm ci` with `npm install` in the Dockerfile, or commit a package-lock.json
fix_before_production.why: The repo has no package-lock.json, so `npm ci` exits with an error and the image never builds.

fix_before_production.title: Use mirrored base images: mirror.gcr.io/library/node:20-alpine and mirror.gcr.io/library/nginx:alpine
fix_before_production.why: Pulling node:20-alpine and nginx:alpine directly from Docker Hub can hit rate limits and fail the build.

fix_before_production.title: Repeat the security headers inside the static-asset location block (or add them with `always` there too)
fix_before_production.why: nginx drops server-level add_header directives in any location that defines its own add_header. JS, CSS and image responses therefore currently go out without X-Frame-Options or X-Content-Type-Options.

verify_after_deploy: GET / on the app URL returns 200 with Content-Type text/html and the page includes a <script> tag pointing at /assets/
GET /some/unknown/route on the app URL returns 200 and the same index.html (SPA fallback via try_files)
GET one of the /assets/*.js files referenced by index.html returns 200 with header `Cache-Control: public, immutable`
GET / response headers include X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
productionPlan.nexlayer_yaml:
application:
  name: cyberpunk-analytics
  pods:
    - name: web
      image: "registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/cyberpunk-analytics-web:planned"
      path: /
      servicePorts:
        - 80
      vars: {}
